before: Runs, text elements and run properties were shared records under their paragraph. Concurrent writes of a paragraph's or run's properties kept one author's whole property container, typing in a run a peer deleted or reformatted at once was lost, two peers splitting or joining the same text kept both copies, and a replacement was written after the text it replaced.
after: Each paragraph's inline content is one shared text: characters carry their run, text element, run properties (one attribute per property) and wrappers as formatting, and other inline elements are embedded records. Concurrent formatting merges per property and character, typing inside a deleted run survives, a moved copy shows once in the last paragraph in document order that holds it, text typed next to text a peer moves to another paragraph follows the move (also after an undo of a split), typed text that Yjs places behind moved characters names its anchor, an embed whose record has not arrived yet waits instead of reporting lost content, and a winning paragraph property container also shows the properties its hidden copies hold, concurrent changes to one drawing keep one value per position, wrap and placement, an undo of a note no longer breaks a later note, and a replica waiting for a held-back update keeps its last complete view instead of reporting an error, two first comments made at once both stay when one is undone, and an undone comment or note stays removed on every replica, a part two peers create at once keeps its content type when one of them undoes it, and a peer's malformed formatting attributes or node kinds cost only formatting, never characters or the room, text typed after a character that is later deleted stays where it was typed, an edit refuses to replace a paragraph text that is still arriving, and comment markers placed around moved text keep it from showing twice, a mark that arrives late updates every copy that reads through it, text typed at the start of a paragraph a peer joins back, or between two concurrent joins of one paragraph, keeps its place, typing where a split was joined back stays when a later split moves the text after it, a paragraph shows each character once, and no replica removes a formatting marker, so text a peer types behind one keeps its run and text element. A notes or numbering part that two peers create at once stays when one of them undoes theirs, and an inline drawing does not show a wrap a peer gave its anchor at the same time. Text with characters outside the basic plane, such as emoji, stays intact on every replica, because no edit lands between the two halves of one. A deletion in a paragraph that holds a hidden copy of the deleted text, as two concurrent joins of one paragraph leave, deletes that copy too. A server that holds the room's document prepares it with `prepareCollaborationServerDocument`, so it never removes a marker either. A tab or picture placed at the end of a paragraph that a split shortened stays there, as typed text does. Typing that an edit copies again, as a join copies a removed paragraph's text back, keeps its original until the copy arrives, so a replica that receives the edit first never shows the text missing. Text that follows a move and is anchored inside other following text of the same paragraph is written once, with its identity. Text a participant deletes stays deleted when another participant moves it, joins it, or undoes a change around it at the same time: each edit records the identities it deletes and does not copy, in the document map `docx-text-deletions-v1`, and the undo of that edit withdraws the record. Drawings in a deleted paragraph go with it. Typing a peer joined into a paragraph that another peer's undo removed shows in the paragraph it was typed in. A room records its size when it is seeded (`freshBytes`) and the generation it belongs to (`roomGeneration`) in its shared metadata. A server compacts a room that has grown past twice its seeded size into a new generation when it loads it, and refuses a client that holds another generation with `room-generation-changed`; clients name their generation in a stateless message before they sync.
reason: The shared node and character representation changed, so released participants cannot read the new paragraph texts, and the rules that repair concurrent structure changed, so for the same shared state they would show different documents. Both sharedSchemaVersion and repairVersion increase, and saved rooms are exported and reseeded.
